payload.report: The yellowish oval lesion within chorioretinal atrophy, combined with high myopia and axial length of 30.0 mm, strongly indicates pathologic myopia degeneration. OCT showing focal scleral ectasia with choroidal obliteration and thinning directly matches this degenerative process, while FA revealing only mild late hyperfluorescence without neovascular leakage excludes active choroidal neovascularization or tumor. These imaging findings support pathologic myopia degeneration with a confidence of 0.92 and effectively refute choroidal neoplasm/tumor (0.05) and inflammatory choroiditis (0.03). The evidence converges on a degenerative myopic etiology, and the diagnosis is sufficiently specific, requiring no further refinement.
